statusDetail: 58/58 atomic checks judged. Representative secondary routes exposed bot verification and a broken login render; these are recorded as observed issues rather than unexecuted checks.

paths.description: Entry/search and mixed listing archetype; tested first load, mobile/desktop, preferences, performance, accessibility, security and memory.
Primary used-car results/listing journey; navigation reached a human-verification state.
Representative vehicle detail; navigation reached a human-verification state.
Editorial/content archetype; navigation reached a human-verification state.
Account/authentication flow; endpoint rendered escaped markup rather than a usable form.

findings.summary: No intrusive pop-ups, interstitials or banners that obscure content on load; overlays are dismissible and content-first.
findings.evidence: first viewport is fully obscured by a consent interstitial before any interaction
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking first-load wall with a compact, content-preserving consent surface where legally possible.

findings.summary: Touch targets are adequately sized and hover-only affordances have a non-hover fallback, and keyboard focus is visible, so the UI works for touch, pointer and keyboard alike.
findings.evidence: focused first link computed outline is none; many links are only 13-18px high
findings.suggestedFix: Add visible :focus-visible styles and enlarge touch targets to at least 24px, preferably 44px.

findings.summary: The page communicates what it is for and exposes the primary next action without requiring users to hunt through decorative content, generic copy, or competing calls to action.
findings.evidence: search/listing purpose exists behind the page, but the blocking consent wall hides it on first load
findings.suggestedFix: Expose the vehicle search and primary next action in the initial usable viewport.

findings.summary: The representative primary flow can be completed end-to-end with predictable steps, no avoidable dead ends, no hidden required information, and no needless detours through modals, account walls, or upsells.
findings.evidence: listing, detail, and article navigations returned a Cloudflare human-verification wall; the login endpoint rendered escaped HTML text
findings.suggestedFix: Tune bot protection and endpoint rendering so normal navigation and sign-in remain completable.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are in the good range: LCP is fast, interaction latency (INP) is low, and CLS is minimal; work is prioritised and deferred sensibly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 12.2s, CLS 0.131 and TBT 230ms; trace measured LCP 6.78s and TBT 2.17s
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP chain, defer non-critical scripts, and break up long tasks.

findings.summary: The main thread is not blocked by long tasks or heavy scripting; work is deferred, chunked, prioritised, or moved off-thread.
findings.evidence: trace found a 2,199ms main-thread task and 2,174ms total blocking time
findings.suggestedFix: Split synchronous page initialization and defer ad/analytics work until idle or consent.

findings.summary: Critical resources are delivered efficiently: cache headers are useful, render-blocking chains are short, fonts do not block or shift text, HTTP delivery is modern, and network dependency trees do not delay the main content.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded five VeryHigh render-blocking stylesheets and several synchronous classic scripts; probe confirmed key scripts lack async/defer
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, reduce font stylesheets, and defer non-critical classic scripts.

findings.summary: The page does not ship large unused or duplicated JavaScript/CSS, avoidable legacy bundles, or third-party code that dominates the load without user value.
findings.evidence: 976KB of script was transferred; ad, analytics, Facebook and chat bundles dominate the 1.58MB load
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or conditionally load third-party bundles after consent/intent.

findings.summary: Interactive elements have accessible names, correct roles, and form fields have labels; images have alt text where meaningful; canvas/expressive content is exposed to assistive technology.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found unnamed links; image audit found 42 images without alt; search text input has no label
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control an accessible name, label search, and add meaningful alt or empty alt for decoration.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is logical, focus order follows reading order, keyboard focus is always visible, and interactive state survives DOM moves.
findings.evidence: visible headings begin at H3 and no visible page H1 exists; focused first link has outline:none
findings.suggestedFix: Restore one visible H1, logical heading order, landmarks, and strong :focus-visible styling.

findings.summary: The experience remains usable when zoomed or reflowed, touch targets are large enough, media has captions or equivalents where needed, and the viewport does not prevent user scaling.
findings.evidence: viewport disables zoom with maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=0; many targets are 13-18px high
findings.suggestedFix: Allow user zoom and increase compact links/touch targets.

findings.summary: Served over HTTPS with a sensible Content-Security-Policy and secure, SameSite cookies; no mixed content or obvious transport/header smells.
findings.evidence: HTTPS/HSTS/nosniff are present, but CSP is missing and 6 of 8 cookies lack Secure
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP and set Secure/SameSite attributes consistently.

findings.summary: No over-collection of user data, no leaky third parties, and analytics/background data collection is minimised and batched rather than chatty or session-wide by default.
findings.evidence: 18 third-party origins and 7 known trackers loaded; 80/82 requests and 1.56MB were classified third-party
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize trackers and gate all non-essential third parties behind consent and user intent.

findings.summary: Permission prompts are requested in context (not on load), and authentication uses modern, phishing-resistant methods (passkeys / WebAuthn) where relevant rather than passwords alone.
findings.evidence: no permission prompt fired on home, but the sign-in endpoint rendered escaped markup and no usable modern-auth surface could be reached
findings.suggestedFix: Repair sign-in and offer a WebAuthn/passkey path alongside appropriate fallback.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are configured where appropriate: HSTS, clickjacking protection (frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options), Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive apps, origin isolation, privacy-preserving third-party cookie posture, and sensible Referrer-Policy / Permissions-Policy.
findings.evidence: CSP and Permissions-Policy are absent; Referrer-Policy is the weak no-referrer-when-downgrade default
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP/frame-ancestors, Permissions-Policy and strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy.

findings.summary: The page behaves robustly at runtime: overlays and menus never get cut off, DOM state survives moves, background work and async dependencies are sequenced and conditional rather than fragile, and initial visibility state is detected correctly.
findings.evidence: representative internal navigations degrade to a bot wall, and login renders escaped markup instead of an interactive form
findings.suggestedFix: Make route/runtime handling robust and ensure challenge/login responses render valid interactive states.

findings.summary: Checkout, subscription, consent, authentication and account-management flows are clear, reversible, and proportionate: pricing and commitments are visible, cancellation is findable, sensitive actions re-authenticate when appropriate, and users are not tricked into continuity.
findings.evidence: sign-in endpoint displays escaped HTML rather than a usable account form, preventing a clear account flow
findings.suggestedFix: Repair the sign-in response, then provide clear recovery and passkey-capable authentication.

findings.summary: Images and decorative assets are optimised and served at appropriate resolutions; decorative pseudo-element imagery and heavy decorative images are resolution-optimised rather than oversized.
findings.evidence: 46/49 images lack responsive srcset, 11 use legacy formats and 46 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded
findings.suggestedFix: Use AVIF/WebP, responsive srcset/sizes, intrinsic dimensions and below-fold lazy loading.

findings.summary: Background work and fetching are not wasteful: background processing is efficient and de-prioritised, and the lightest technique that achieves the result is preferred over heavy or redundant work.
findings.evidence: trace found 2.17s blocking time and HAR shows ad/analytics work loading before user intent
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritize or remove background ad/analytics work and load conditionally.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts, fonts, video, audio, animation and heavy media are proportionate to the user value they provide; autoplay or background media is avoided unless essential and resource use is cached or deferred where possible.
findings.evidence: third parties account for 1.56MB and 80 of 82 requests, including ad, analytics, Facebook and chat code
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget and defer non-essential media/scripts until consent or interaction.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-color-scheme: a usable dark mode exists and is driven by the user's preference (color-scheme / prefers-color-scheme / light-dark()), not hard-coded light only.
findings.evidence: screenshot under emulated dark mode is pixel-identical to light mode; no color-scheme CSS was found
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme and theme tokens driven by prefers-color-scheme/light-dark().

findings.summary: Overlays and rich controls use the right primitive: popover (with declarative light-dismiss) for transient UI, dialog for modal flows, details for disclosure, native-but-branded selects and pickers, rather than ad-hoc divs.
findings.evidence: probe found 3 custom modal-role elements but zero native dialog, popover, or details elements
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog/popover/details with declarative dismissal and correct focus management.

findings.summary: Minimise non-content chrome and borders so the content is the focus, not the application frame; expressive/decorative visuals serve the content rather than crowd it.
findings.evidence: consent chrome consumes the whole first viewport and persistent header/chat controls compete with marketplace content
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce persistent chrome and keep the first viewport focused on search and listings.

findings.summary: No cumulative layout shift from late content (images, banners, fonts) that arrives without reserved space.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.131 despite the shorter layout observation measuring 0.012
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for late content and use stable font/image sizing.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI meet WCAG colour-contrast minimums against their background.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found white VIN badge text at 3.24:1, below the required 4.5:1
findings.suggestedFix: Darken badge backgrounds or adjust text color to meet WCAG contrast.

findings.summary: Valid doctype and charset, images sized with correct aspect ratio, no deprecated APIs misused, and CSS/HTML are well structured and not needlessly repetitive. (HTTPS, CSP and permission hygiene are judged under be-private-and-secure, not here.)
findings.evidence: doctype/charset are valid, but image audit found 43 images without width/height and 46 without srcset
findings.suggestedFix: Provide intrinsic image dimensions and responsive srcset/sizes.

findings.summary: Links are crawlable (real href), there is a viewport meta tag, robots does not block indexing, and link text is descriptive.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found a feedback anchor with no href; robots and viewport otherwise exist
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href URLs for all navigational links and retain descriptive link text.

findings.summary: Where the page represents an article, product, organization, event, place or other rich entity, structured data and share-preview metadata accurately describe the visible content.
findings.evidence: Open Graph title/description/url exist, but no JSON-LD was present for marketplace/product entities
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org JSON-LD for Organization, WebSite/SearchAction and listing/product entities.

findings.summary: Input is assisted, not obstructed: correct autocomplete tokens so address, payment, sign-in and sign-up fields autofill, and inputs are highlighted/sized to help the user rather than trip them up.
findings.evidence: primary text search has autocomplete=off, no name and no accessible label
findings.suggestedFix: Name and label search inputs and avoid disabling browser input assistance without a specific need.

findings.summary: Where it makes sense, the site exposes structured, safe capabilities to agents via WebMCP tools, agentic forms, and agentic JavaScript tools rather than leaving agents to scrape and guess.
findings.evidence: robots.txt explicitly blocks anthropic-ai, Claude-Web and Applebot-Extended; no JSON-LD or agent tool registration was found
findings.suggestedFix: Choose and document an AI-crawler policy; expose safe structured listing/search capabilities and metadata where desired.

findings.summary: State and route changes use View Transitions (including same-document, cross-document and scroll-driven/staggered) rather than instant, jarring swaps.
findings.evidence: CSS/animation probe found no View Transition rules or animations for state/route changes
findings.suggestedFix: Use progressive View Transitions for route and major state changes.

findings.summary: Gesture-driven interactions and entry/exit motion feel native (declarative overscroll/scroll-snap, physics-based easing, animating to intrinsic sizes, pull/swipe gestures) rather than fighting the platform with custom pointer handlers.
findings.evidence: content carousels and long mobile surfaces expose no scroll-snap/overscroll declarative gesture CSS
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-snap and declarative overscroll behavior for carousels and gesture surfaces.

findings.summary: Sticky/affixed UI reacts to scroll state and position (e.g. the new scroll-state(scrolled) query, shrinking headers, progress indicators) so chrome responds to position instead of static or JS-driven toggling.
findings.evidence: long 6,122px page uses static header chrome; no scroll-state/progress CSS was found
findings.suggestedFix: Make sticky chrome respond to scroll state and provide progress/affordance cues.

findings.summary: Navigation and in-page jumps guide attention (highlight effects, scroll/carousel markers, directional transitions, drill-down and drawer navigation) so the user can follow where focus moved.
findings.evidence: navigation/state changes expose no directional transition, marker, highlight, or focus cue
findings.suggestedFix: Add clear focus/selection cues and directional transitions around navigation changes.

findings.summary: Components adapt to their container with container queries (incl. anchored container queries) and content/state-based styling where reused at different sizes, not only global viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: CSS probe found no container queries or container-type; adaptation relies on a separate mobile surface
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reusable search, card, and navigation components.
